correctness.rationale: Every cyclic binary de Bruijn word of order five corresponds bijectively to a 32-edge Euler circuit anchored at the unique 00000 edge. Each incoming/outgoing local-pairing assignment is explicitly enumerated (65536); the independent anchored depth-first Eulerian generator enumerates all alternatives; both return exactly the same 2048 canonical words, each checked for all five-bit windows. Three mathematically equivalent but computationally different exact integer autocorrelation formulas agree at every independent lag for every word. Grouping complete signatures yields 30 fibers of size two, 495 of size four, and one of size eight; grouping reversal-complement symmetries identifies exactly two fibers spanning two inequivalent orbits. The 521 versus 526 prefix-signature counts through lags twelve and thirteen, together with a concrete pair distinguished at lag thirteen, prove both recovery sufficiency and sharpness within the finite domain. The executable file and both CSV files in this package reproduce every count; finite exhaustive claims are not extrapolated to higher order.

value.rationale: Cyclic autocorrelation/power spectrum is a natural, established reconstruction invariant; binary order-five de Bruijn cycles provide an explicitly finite yet nontrivial universal-cycle family. Classifying complete fibers rather than a scalar summary resolves the precise ambiguity of phase retrieval: only two non-symmetry ambiguity pairs survive among 528 symmetry classes. The sharp nine-observation (lags 5–13) recovery of the entire power spectrum provides a motivated exact compressed-data characterization, and the exceptional representative pairs are concrete witnesses. A full independently regenerated finite census provides a reproducible benchmark; the finite natural classification is valuable without claiming a higher-order theorem.
